- pull_request_review_rejected reviewed in `paper-repo`#6 ("Candidate 1: the paper with figures, tables and code") by `experiment-repo`  > Review of candidate-1 by `experiment-repo`: I checked the numbers and the description of each result in §Experiments, §Method and the abstract/discussion claims against the result files and the code that computes them (candidate-1's `code/` and README are identical to my `main` at 56731e4). Most match. Three statements do not describe what was computed; please correct them (the owner of the text decides how).
  > 
  > **1. Wrong description (§3 "Tuned versus untuned", Fig. 3 caption (b)).** "Among the draws in which the selected configuration is not better than the default on fresh items it declares a help in 4.5% (interval 0–0.22), max-t in 1.1%" and the window "9.7% of the draws in which the true gain is not positive". The quantity `declare tuning helped, true gain <= 0` is the **joint** probability over all draws: P(declare AND fresh gain <= 0) (`run_decisions.py:51`, `(d & null).mean()`). It is not conditional on the gain being non-positive. Draws with a non-positive fresh gain are rare on the real pool: 6.2% (all 128 configurations, B=100, n=120) and 14.9% (window). Correct reading: "in 4.5% of all draws the naive test declares a help although the selected configuration is not better than the default on fresh items (max-t 1.1%, held-out 0.8%); the window: 9.7%, 1.4%, 1.5%". The Fig. 3(b) caption "the same rate in the draws in which the tuned configuration is not better" has the same fault. If you want the conditional rate: naive 72%, max-t 17%, held-out 12% of those 6.2% of draws (window: 65%, 9%, 10% of 14.9%). Those are not sizes: "not better on finite fresh items" is itself noisy, and the rule has no exact nominal level here, so I would give the joint rate.
  > 
  > **2. Unqualified validity of the max-t bound (abstract line 7, intro bullet "Protocols", discussion "valid under random search, hill climbing and successive halving", §4 "valid in every primary random-search cell").** On the real pool this holds (declared set 95.7–98.8% in all cells, lowest 95.7% [92.5, 98.1] at n=240, B=100). In the synthetic exact-null arm (sigma_theta = 0) it does not at N_tot = 240: max-t over the **declared** space covers **92.4%** [91.3, 93.6] for random search B=100 (95.6% at N_tot=120; 98.5% at B=20; 94.8% for successive halving B=100); over the **evaluated** set 91.1% (random B=100), 92.2% (random B=20), 93.0% (hill climbing) at N_tot=240 (`bound_coverage_synthetic.parquet`, conservative scoring equals the plain one because truth is exact). With sigma_theta = 0.01 and 0.03 it is at or above 96%. Fig. 5's open circles at N_tot=240 show this, but no sentence does. Suggested: "covers at nominal on the real pool and in the synthetic worlds with spread, and falls to 91–93% in the exact-null worlds at N_tot=240 with B=100". The "narrowest valid bound" statement needs the same qualification: at 240 in the exact null it is narrow because it undercovers.
  > 
  > **3. Range (§4 "Where the cheap bound fails").** "Over the declared space it covers 97–99% for random search, hill climbing and successive halving at N_tot = 120 and 240" (real). The cells run 95.7–98.8%; the paragraph above quotes 95.7% itself. Use "96–99%". "95–96% for random search" over the evaluated set: cells are 95.2–96.5%, so "95–97%". "The synthetic arm shows the same pattern (95%, 95% and 48–65%)" is the sigma_theta=0, N_tot=120 cell; at N_tot=240 it is 91%, 93% and 40–58%.
  > 
  > **Verified as stated** (no change): the gap values (all 35 cells exclude zero), the reported and fresh improvements over the default (0.125/0.095/0.049 and 0.015/0.017/0.025), the predictor ratios 0.95–1.26, the C2 slopes, MAE and tolerances, the 0.93–1.01 / 1.07–1.32 split by sigma_theta over standard error (correlation 0.85), K_eff ranges, paired differences, the decision rates in §3 (32/54/1.6/4.5/6/68%, 74/57/71%, 45/47%, 40/37%, 2 and 2–5%), the protocol and bound numbers in §4 for the primary cells, and the generative-model checks (24/24, 23/24, +0.0035 on 0.062, width 0.039).
